claim: There is an urgent need to develop new methods for male contraception.
source: There is an urgent need to develop new methods for male contraception, however a major barrier to drug discovery has been the lack of validated targets and the absence of an effective high-throughput phenotypic screening system.
evidence: This is a statement of need in the abstract, supported by the context of the manuscript discussing the contraceptive gap.

claim: A major barrier to drug discovery for male contraception has been the lack of validated targets.
source: There is an urgent need to develop new methods for male contraception, however a major barrier to drug discovery has been the lack of validated targets and the absence of an effective high-throughput phenotypic screening system.
evidence: This is stated as a known barrier in the field.

claim: A major barrier to drug discovery for male contraception has been the absence of an effective high-throughput phenotypic screening system.
source: There is an urgent need to develop new methods for male contraception, however a major barrier to drug discovery has been the lack of validated targets and the absence of an effective high-throughput phenotypic screening system.
evidence: This is stated as a known barrier in the field.

claim: The authors developed a fully-automated robotic screening platform for evaluating compound activity against human sperm function.
source: To address this deficit, we developed a fully-automated robotic screening platform that provided quantitative evaluation of compound activity against two key attributes of human sperm function: motility and acrosome reaction.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, describing the platform development.

claim: The screening platform provides quantitative evaluation of compound activity against human sperm motility.
source: To address this deficit, we developed a fully-automated robotic screening platform that provided quantitative evaluation of compound activity against two key attributes of human sperm function: motility and acrosome reaction.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the platform.

claim: The screening platform provides quantitative evaluation of compound activity against human sperm acrosome reaction.
source: To address this deficit, we developed a fully-automated robotic screening platform that provided quantitative evaluation of compound activity against two key attributes of human sperm function: motility and acrosome reaction.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the platform.

claim: The ReFRAME repurposing library comprises nearly all the small molecules that have been approved or have undergone clinical development, or have significant preclinical profiling.
source: In order to accelerate contraceptive development, we screened the comprehensive collection of 12,000 molecules that make up the ReFRAME repurposing library, comprising nearly all the small molecules that have been approved or have undergone clinical development, or have significant preclinical profiling.
evidence: This describes the composition of the ReFRAME library, supported by citation to Janes et al., 2018.

claim: The authors screened 12,000 molecules from the ReFRAME repurposing library.
source: In order to accelerate contraceptive development, we screened the comprehensive collection of 12,000 molecules that make up the ReFRAME repurposing library, comprising nearly all the small molecules that have been approved or have undergone clinical development, or have significant preclinical profiling.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding of the study.

claim: The authors identified several compounds that potently inhibit sperm motility.
source: We identified several compounds that potently inhibit motility representing either novel drug candidates or routes to target identification.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the screening study.

claim: More than 214 million women in developing countries have an unmet need for contraception.
source: For example, it is estimated that more than 214 million women in developing countries have an unmet need for contraception which results in 89 million unintended pregnancies and 48 million abortions every year, with substantial impacts on maternal and child health and poverty levels (Guttmacher Institute, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guttmacher Institute, 2017.

claim: Unmet contraceptive need results in 89 million unintended pregnancies every year.
source: For example, it is estimated that more than 214 million women in developing countries have an unmet need for contraception which results in 89 million unintended pregnancies and 48 million abortions every year, with substantial impacts on maternal and child health and poverty levels (Guttmacher Institute, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guttmacher Institute, 2017.

claim: Unmet contraceptive need results in 48 million abortions every year.
source: For example, it is estimated that more than 214 million women in developing countries have an unmet need for contraception which results in 89 million unintended pregnancies and 48 million abortions every year, with substantial impacts on maternal and child health and poverty levels (Guttmacher Institute, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guttmacher Institute, 2017.

claim: No effective, reversible and widely available form of contraception has been developed for men since the condom.
source: However, it is noticeable that no effective, reversible and widely available form of contraception has been developed for men since the condom and as such the burden falls largely on the woman.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about the state of male contraception.

claim: Spermatozoa don't divide, transcribe or translate.
source: Developing a drug for any purpose is difficult but one that blocks sperm function is a particular challenge as spermatozoa don't divide, transcribe or translate, have specialized organelles, are highly motile and continually produced in large numbers (~100 million per day).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about spermatozoa.

claim: Spermatozoa have specialized organelles.
source: Developing a drug for any purpose is difficult but one that blocks sperm function is a particular challenge as spermatozoa don't divide, transcribe or translate, have specialized organelles, are highly motile and continually produced in large numbers (~100 million per day).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about spermatozoa.

claim: Spermatozoa are highly motile.
source: Developing a drug for any purpose is difficult but one that blocks sperm function is a particular challenge as spermatozoa don't divide, transcribe or translate, have specialized organelles, are highly motile and continually produced in large numbers (~100 million per day).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about spermatozoa.

claim: Spermatozoa are continually produced in large numbers (~100 million per day).
source: Developing a drug for any purpose is difficult but one that blocks sperm function is a particular challenge as spermatozoa don't divide, transcribe or translate, have specialized organelles, are highly motile and continually produced in large numbers (~100 million per day).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about spermatozoa production.

claim: Low sperm motility is a common cause of male infertility.
source: Low sperm motility is a common cause of male infertility (Samplaski et al., 2019) indicating that targeting this process should yield effective drugs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Samplaski et al., 2019.

claim: Targeting sperm motility should yield effective contraceptive drugs.
source: Low sperm motility is a common cause of male infertility (Samplaski et al., 2019) indicating that targeting this process should yield effective drugs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between motility and fertility.

claim: CatSper is a potential sperm-specific contraceptive drug target.
source: Though some potential sperm-specific contraceptive drug targets, such as the calcium channel CatSper, have been identified (Lishko and Mannowetz, 2018), our relatively poor understanding of spermatozoon biology makes target-agnostic, or phenotypic strategies more attractive (Barratt et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lishko and Mannowetz, 2018.

claim: Phenotypic drug discovery is undergoing a renaissance in a number of therapeutic areas.
source: Phenotypic drug discovery is undergoing a renaissance in a number of therapeutic areas because it can uncover novel biology in an unbiased way.
evidence: This is stated as a trend in drug discovery.

claim: Phenotypic drug discovery can uncover novel biology in an unbiased way.
source: Phenotypic drug discovery is undergoing a renaissance in a number of therapeutic areas because it can uncover novel biology in an unbiased way.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of phenotypic approaches.

claim: Retrospective analysis shows phenotypic approaches are more successful in first-in-class medicine discovery than previously appreciated.
source: Retrospective analysis of drug approvals shows the approach to be more successful in first-in-class medicine discovery than previously appreciated (Swinney and Anthony, 2011; Moffat et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Swinney and Anthony, 2011 and Moffat et al., 2017.

claim: The platform allows for identification of relatively fast-acting compounds.
source: Our automated platform (Figure 1A) allows for the identification of relatively fast-acting compounds with a rapid plate-processing time (~75 minutes/ 384-well plate), where the motility assay runs for ~30 min followed directly by the AR assay (~45 min).
evidence: This describes a capability of the developed platform.

claim: The platform has a rapid plate-processing time of approximately 75 minutes per 384-well plate.
source: Our automated platform (Figure 1A) allows for the identification of relatively fast-acting compounds with a rapid plate-processing time (~75 minutes/ 384-well plate), where the motility assay runs for ~30 min followed directly by the AR assay (~45 min).
evidence: This is a measured characteristic of the platform.

claim: The motility assay runs for approximately 30 minutes.
source: Our automated platform (Figure 1A) allows for the identification of relatively fast-acting compounds with a rapid plate-processing time (~75 minutes/ 384-well plate), where the motility assay runs for ~30 min followed directly by the AR assay (~45 min).
evidence: This is a measured characteristic of the motility assay.

claim: The AR assay runs for approximately 45 minutes.
source: Our automated platform (Figure 1A) allows for the identification of relatively fast-acting compounds with a rapid plate-processing time (~75 minutes/ 384-well plate), where the motility assay runs for ~30 min followed directly by the AR assay (~45 min).
evidence: This is a measured characteristic of the AR assay.

claim: Automated cell tracking allows kinetic parameter quantification on >200 cells per well.
source: Automated cell tracking (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B) using time-lapse images allowed kinetic parameter quantification on >200 cells/well (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a measured capability of the tracking system, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The kinetics from the platform show good agreement with clinical systems.
source: The kinetics show good agreement with clinical systems (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and a comparable distribution was observed between experimental days, plates and positions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with any small differences between days stemming from donor pool variance.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Spermatozoa were found to be tolerant to DMSO concentrations of 0.0625%–0.1%.
source: Importantly, spermatozoa were found to be tolerant to the DMSO concentrations used in our screening program (0.0625%–0.1% Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Only a small decrease in motility (~10%) was observed after four plates were screened.
source: To determine the optimal screening batch size untreated spermatozoa were dispensed every 30 min for 150 min observing only a small decrease in motility (~10%) after four plates were screened (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The ReFRAME library contains 11,968 compounds.
source: The ReFRAME library (11,968 compounds) was supplied in 'assay-ready' imaging plates and was solubilised prior to addition of sperm.
evidence: This is a stated fact about the library screened.

claim: High assay quality was achieved throughout with a Z'-factor between 0.4–0.8.
source: High assay quality was achieved throughout with a Z'-factor between 0.4–0.8 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a measured quality metric shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 63 putative hit compounds decreased motility based on a hit selection cut-off of >15% reduction in motility.
source: A total of 63 putative hit compounds decreased motility to varying degrees based on a hit selection cut-off of >15% reduction in motility (Figure 2A with examples in Figure 2C,D,F,G and Video 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a primary screening result shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 14 compounds were selected as putative AR+ hits.
source: 14 compounds were selected as putative AR+ hits (Figure 3A with examples in B, C).
evidence: This is a primary screening result shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 29 motility hit compounds were confirmed with resupplied material in dose-response experiments.
source: Motility hits were confirmed with resupplied material in dose-response experiments. There was a dose-dependent decrease in motility for 29 compounds (46% hit confirmation rate), with EC50 values as low as 0.05 µM and effect sizes ranging from 15–100% (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a confirmation result from dose-response experiments.

claim: The hit confirmation rate for motility compounds was 46%.
source: There was a dose-dependent decrease in motility for 29 compounds (46% hit confirmation rate), with EC50 values as low as 0.05 µM and effect sizes ranging from 15–100% (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the confirmation experiments.

claim: Confirmed motility hits had EC50 values as low as 0.05 µM.
source: There was a dose-dependent decrease in motility for 29 compounds (46% hit confirmation rate), with EC50 values as low as 0.05 µM and effect sizes ranging from 15–100% (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a measured potency from dose-response experiments.

claim: Confirmed motility hits had effect sizes ranging from 15–100%.
source: There was a dose-dependent decrease in motility for 29 compounds (46% hit confirmation rate), with EC50 values as low as 0.05 µM and effect sizes ranging from 15–100% (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a measured efficacy from dose-response experiments.

claim: Disulfiram was a confirmed hit with 70% maximum reduction at 10 µM.
source: Amongst the confirmed hits were the aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor, Disulfiram (70% maximum reduction at 10 µM) and a putative platelet aggregation inhibitor, KF-4939 (100% max. reduction; EC50 = 0.49 μM), and a range of other compounds having very modest effect and/or showing low potency (See Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a specific hit result from dose-response experiments.

claim: KF-4939 was a confirmed hit with 100% maximum reduction and EC50 = 0.49 μM.
source: Amongst the confirmed hits were the aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor, Disulfiram (70% maximum reduction at 10 µM) and a putative platelet aggregation inhibitor, KF-4939 (100% max. reduction; EC50 = 0.49 μM), and a range of other compounds having very modest effect and/or showing low potency (See Figure 2—source data 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a specific hit result from dose-response experiments.

claim: Only a small recovery of motility was observed after wash out of Disulfiram.
source: In order to test reversibility, wash out experiments were performed. Only a small recovery of motility was observed, after wash out of Disulfiram (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result from washout experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: 9 of the resupplied AR compounds had a dose-dependent effect with EC50 values as low as 0.4 µM.
source: In the AR screen, 9 of the resupplied compounds had a dose-dependent effect with EC50 values as low as 0.4 µM (See Figure 3—source data 2, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a result from AR dose-response experiments.

claim: None of the AR hits were found to be true positives after orthogonal assay triaging.
source: However, following the orthogonal assay triaging we implemented to eliminate assay interference compounds, none of the AR hits were found to be true positives (see examples in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) despite the primary screen showing good assay robustness.
evidence: This is a result from triaging experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The hit rate of approximately 0.2% in the motility assay is typical for a cell-based assay.
source: In the motility assay the hit rate of ~0.2% is typical for a cell-based assay, however surprisingly a relatively high number of hits were not deemed suitable for compound progression.
evidence: This is a comparison to typical cell-based assay performance.

claim: Disulfiram is a drug that has long been used for treating alcohol dependency.
source: One is Disulfiram (70% reduction at 10 μM) a drug that is well tolerated, has long been used for treating alcohol dependency and has previously been shown to inhibit sperm motility (Lal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Disulfiram, supported by citation.

claim: Disulfiram has previously been shown to inhibit sperm motility.
source: One is Disulfiram (70% reduction at 10 μM) a drug that is well tolerated, has long been used for treating alcohol dependency and has previously been shown to inhibit sperm motility (Lal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lal et al., 2016.

claim: 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) has been identified as a target for disulfiram.
source: One recent report identified 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) as a target for disulfiram (Spillier et al., 2019) whilst another identified NLP4, a subunit of VCP/p97 segregase (Skrott et al., 2017; Skrott et al., 2019) although the relevance of either to sperm function is unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Spillier et al., 2019.

claim: NLP4, a subunit of VCP/p97 segregase, has been identified as a target for disulfiram.
source: One recent report identified 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) as a target for disulfiram (Spillier et al., 2019) whilst another identified NLP4, a subunit of VCP/p97 segregase (Skrott et al., 2017; Skrott et al., 2019) although the relevance of either to sperm function is unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Skrott et al., 2017 and Skrott et al., 2019.

claim: PAF has been used to improve sperm function in male infertility treatments.
source: The identification of KF-4939, a putative platelet aggregation factor (PAF) inhibitor, as a potent hit (100% max. reduction EC50 = 0.5 µM) may also be of interest since PAF has been used to improve sperm function in male infertility treatments (Roudebush et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roudebush et al., 2004.

claim: Bismuth ethanedithiol was a potent hit with 98% maximum reduction and EC50 = 2.5 μM.
source: Further thiol-containing compounds, bismuth ethanedithiol (98% max reduction; EC50 = 2.5 μM) and the anti-fungal benzothiazole, Ticlatone (96% max. reduction EC50 = 4.4 µM) were also potent hits, suggesting free cysteines in, as yet, unidentified protein(s), may play a critical role in motility.
evidence: This is a specific hit result from dose-response experiments.

claim: Ticlatone was a potent hit with 96% maximum reduction and EC50 = 4.4 µM.
source: Further thiol-containing compounds, bismuth ethanedithiol (98% max reduction; EC50 = 2.5 μM) and the anti-fungal benzothiazole, Ticlatone (96% max. reduction EC50 = 4.4 µM) were also potent hits, suggesting free cysteines in, as yet, unidentified protein(s), may play a critical role in motility.
evidence: This is a specific hit result from dose-response experiments.

claim: Free cysteines in unidentified protein(s) may play a critical role in sperm motility.
source: Further thiol-containing compounds, bismuth ethanedithiol (98% max reduction; EC50 = 2.5 μM) and the anti-fungal benzothiazole, Ticlatone (96% max. reduction EC50 = 4.4 µM) were also potent hits, suggesting free cysteines in, as yet, unidentified protein(s), may play a critical role in motility.
evidence: This is inferred from the activity of thiol-containing compounds.

claim: Resquimod (R848) has been shown to preferentially reduce the motility of X chromosome-bearing mouse sperm by suppressing ATP production.
source: Of interest is the observation that the Toll-like receptor 7/8 ligand (Resquimod; R848), recently shown to preferentially reduce the motility of X chromosome-bearing mouse sperm by suppressing ATP production (Umehara et al., 2019), was a hit, demonstrating that this phenotypic screening approach has the potential to uncover new aspects of sperm biology.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Umehara et al., 2019.

claim: Resquimod (R848) was a hit in the motility screen.
source: Of interest is the observation that the Toll-like receptor 7/8 ligand (Resquimod; R848), recently shown to preferentially reduce the motility of X chromosome-bearing mouse sperm by suppressing ATP production (Umehara et al., 2019), was a hit, demonstrating that this phenotypic screening approach has the potential to uncover new aspects of sperm biology.
evidence: This is a screening result.

claim: The phenotypic screening approach has the potential to uncover new aspects of sperm biology.
source: Of interest is the observation that the Toll-like receptor 7/8 ligand (Resquimod; R848), recently shown to preferentially reduce the motility of X chromosome-bearing mouse sperm by suppressing ATP production (Umehara et al., 2019), was a hit, demonstrating that this phenotypic screening approach has the potential to uncover new aspects of sperm biology.
evidence: This is inferred from the identification of Resquimod as a hit.

claim: A large number of compounds had a significant positive effect on sperm motility.
source: Conversely however, we did observe a large number of compounds (Figure 2A) that had a significant positive effect on sperm motility which may be target agonists as well as potential start points for treating men with low sperm motility.
evidence: This is observed in the screening data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The platform utilises a Yokogawa CV7000 Cell Voyager high-throughput microscope.
source: The platform utilises a Yokogawa CV7000 Cell Voyager high-throughput microscope able to image 384 multiwell plates under full environmental control acquiring timelapse images at a sufficiently high speed (~48 fps)_to capture the fast-moving sperm for tracking analysis.
evidence: This describes the equipment used in the platform.

claim: The microscope can acquire timelapse images at approximately 48 fps.
source: The platform utilises a Yokogawa CV7000 Cell Voyager high-throughput microscope able to image 384 multiwell plates under full environmental control acquiring timelapse images at a sufficiently high speed (~48 fps)_to capture the fast-moving sperm for tracking analysis.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the microscope.

claim: All experiments were performed on non-capacitated sperm.
source: We chose to perform all experiments on non-capacitated sperm as this condition is the most consistent, less prone to donor-effects and is closer to the state in which the sperm will be when they would be encountering the male contraceptive drug.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions used.

claim: Non-capacitated sperm is the most consistent condition and less prone to donor-effects.
source: We chose to perform all experiments on non-capacitated sperm as this condition is the most consistent, less prone to donor-effects and is closer to the state in which the sperm will be when they would be encountering the male contraceptive drug.
evidence: This is the rationale for choosing non-capacitated sperm.

claim: Samples were routinely pooled from 3 to 5 donors for use in each screening batch run.
source: We routinely pooled samples after DGC from 3 to 5 donors for use in each screening batch run in order to reduce donor-to-donor variability.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Donor pooling was done to reduce donor-to-donor variability.
source: We routinely pooled samples after DGC from 3 to 5 donors for use in each screening batch run in order to reduce donor-to-donor variability.
evidence: This is the rationale for pooling donors.

claim: Approximately 10,000 spermatozoa were dispensed per well.
source: Approximately 10,000 spermatozoa (10 μl) were dispensed per well using a MultiDrop Combi (ThermoFisher) into pre-warmed assay-ready plates.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Spermatozoa were incubated with compounds for 10 minutes prior to imaging.
source: Spermatozoa were incubated with the compounds for 10 mins (thus favouring fast acting compounds) at 37°C in the CV7000 microscope prior to the commencement of imaging.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Time-lapse image series were acquired at 24 frames in 0.5 seconds.
source: Using a 20x lens with bright field illumination (0.11 ms exposure, 3% lamp power), time-lapse image series were acquired (24 frame in 0.5 s) at two positions per well (with a 400 μm gap between positions to eliminate double counting of sperm).
evidence: This describes the imaging parameters.

claim: Image acquisition across a 384-well plate takes approximately 17 minutes.
source: Image acquisition across a 384-well plate with such settings takes ~ 17 min.
evidence: This is a measured time for image acquisition.

claim: A Python implementation of the Crocker and Grier particle tracking algorithm was employed.
source: A Python implementation of the particle tracking algorithm originally developed by others (Crocker and Grier, 1996) was employed (Trackpy v0.4.1 Allan, 2018).
evidence: This describes the computational method used, supported by citations.

claim: Image data can be processed within 30 minutes using a standard desktop PC.
source: The image data (~17,000 files amounting to 21 GB per plate) can be processed within 30 min using a standard desktop PC (Intel Core i5-6600 CPU, 3.3 GHz, 8 Gb RAM) and can also be parallelized on a compute cluster with minimal effort.
evidence: This is a measured processing time.

claim: The flow cytometry assay employs Alexa488-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PNA).
source: A flow cytometry-based assay was developed employing an iQue Screener (Sartorius) with Alexa488-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PNA) (Mortimer et al., 1987) and general sperm viability (using propidium iodide, Pi).
evidence: This describes the assay reagents, supported by citation.

claim: The flow cytometry assay uses propidium iodide for sperm viability assessment.
source: A flow cytometry-based assay was developed employing an iQue Screener (Sartorius) with Alexa488-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PNA) (Mortimer et al., 1987) and general sperm viability (using propidium iodide, Pi).
evidence: This describes the assay reagents.

claim: Sample processing time is about 25 minutes per 384-well plate for the flow cytometry assay.
source: After addition of dyes, plates were incubated for 10 min at 37°C in the SteriStore before sampling using an iQue Screener (2 s sip time per well with pump setting of 45 rpm). This resulted in a sample processing time of about 25 min per 384-well plate.
evidence: This is a measured processing time.

claim: Pristimerin was used as a positive control for the motility assay at a final concentration of 20 µM.
source: For the motility assay DMSO was used as a vehicle control (negative control) and Pristimerin (Merck, Cat. No. 530070, stored as 10 mM stock in DMSO; final concentration of 20 µM) as a positive control.
evidence: This describes the control conditions.

claim: A23187 was used as a positive control for the acrosome assay at a final concentration of 10 µM.
source: For the acrosome assay we added a calcium ionophore (A23187, Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. No. C7522, stored as 10 mM stock in DMSO, used at a final concentration of 10 µM) as a positive control and DMSO was added to wells as a negative control to be at the same final concentration as that present in the compound-containing wells (0.0625%).
evidence: This describes the control conditions.

claim: The final concentration of DMSO in each screening well was 0.0625%.
source: With the addition of the media containing sperm (10 μl) the final concentration of DMSO in each well was 0.0625%.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Compounds were screened at a final assay concentration of approximately 6 μM.
source: Compounds dissolved in DMSO were spotted (12.5 nL, final assay concentration ~ 6 μM) into 384-well black-sided optical imaging plates (CellCarrier, PerkinElmer) at CALIBR and were shipped on dry ice to the screening centre in Dundee and stored at −20 °C until required.
evidence: This describes the screening concentration.

claim: Dose-response curves were performed with 8-point curves starting at 10 μM highest concentration.
source: Assay-ready 384-well CellCarrier plates with 8-point curves (10 μM highest concentration) were resupplied by CALIBR in duplicate and processed as described above.
evidence: This describes the dose-response experimental design.

claim: Washout experiments were conducted at two timepoints using non-capacitating conditions.
source: In order to assess the ability of sperm cells to recover motility after Disulfiram removal, wash-out experiments were conducted at two timepoints using non-capacitating conditions.
evidence: This describes the washout experimental design.

claim: Disulfiram was tested at 10 μM final concentration in washout experiments.
source: After this initial incubation period, Disulfiram (10 μM final concentration) or vehicle control (DMSO to 0.1% final concentration) were added and incubated at 37°C for 20 min.
evidence: This describes the washout experimental conditions.

claim: Washout experiments were performed on three separated days, utilising different donors to make up the pooled sample.
source: Wash-out experiments were performed on three separated days, utilising different donors to make up the pooled sample.
evidence: This describes the washout experimental design.
